 3d ago 01.41 EST Ivor has been back in touch with the answer to his riddle between the 36th and 37th overs: five England players have played for the Hobart Hurricanes and no Australians [from today’s two XIs]. Can you name them?
 Before I check his email I ticked off what I’m sure are the four easier answers in Harry Brook, Jofra Archer, Will Jacks and Jordan Cox. But happy to admit I’m stumped on the fifth.
 Share 3d ago 01.40 EST 45th over: England 295-7 (Jacks 41, Atkinson 1) Jack Edwards has been used sparingly but is back for a fourth over and dismisses the dangerous Curran. Gus Atkinson comes to the crease and is immediately off the mark with a straight drive and Jacks mimics the stroke for two more.
 Share 3d ago 01.38 EST WICKET! Curran c sub (Scott) b Edwards 19 (England 292-7)
 Sam Curran has been hitting them sweetly but now fails to readjust his stroke for the slower ball and picks out sub fielder Liam Scott on the deep square rope.
 Share 3d ago 01.33 EST 44th over: England 290-6 (Jacks 38, Curran 18) Bartlett returns to the attack for the first time since spending time off the ground with a leg issue. Not enough overs left to get through all of the five he still has remaining after this one but spin has become the order of the day anyway. Bartlett starts with a slower ball that Jacks drives back down the ground for two. Curran clips a fuller delivery off his pads to the deep mid-wicket rope. That was in the air but never in real danger.
 Share 3d ago 01.28 EST 43rd over: England 280-6 (Jacks 34, Curran 13) Curran immediately takes a liking to Edwards’ seamers as he picks up a slower ball and dispatches it over mid-off for four. The all-rounder finds two more with a well-paced shot along the ground to long-on then adds another with a prod to point.
 Share 3d ago 01.24 EST 42nd over: England 272-6 (Jacks 33, Curran 6) Jacks leans back and waits for Connolly’s delivery to come to him before unleashing a sublime drive over cover for four. Four more singles make it another good over for the tourists.
 Share 3d ago 01.21 EST 41st over: England 264-6 (Jacks 27, Curran 4) Renshaw bowls out his overs and England might be pleased to see him off. Six singles from the over as Australia have five players in the deep and the part-timer finishes with 3 for 51.
 Share 3d ago 01.18 EST 40th over: England 258-6 (Jacks 24, Curran 1) Jacks takes over from Duckett as the main aggressor as he clobbers Beardman over cover with a flat bat to the rope. Beardman almost gets immediate revenge as Jacks mistimes a drive that flies towards Edwards before bouncing just in front of the fielder.
 Share 3d ago 01.13 EST WICKET! Duckett c Inglis b Renshaw 133 (England 251-6)
 Renshaw returns and picks up the crucial wicket of Ben Duckett. The England opener has laid the groundwork for his attack with a slow sweep over the rope but ends the over getting a top edge that pops up for Inglis to claim next to the stumps. Duckett’s knock ends with 15 boundaries and three sixes from 115 balls.
 39th over: England 251-6 (Jacks 19, Curran 0) 
 Share 3d ago 01.10 EST 38th over: England 239-5 (Duckett 124, Jacks 16) Beardman has found a better line and length in this spell as he restricts England to a trio of singles. A slower ball shows he has an array of weapons and Jacks is fortunate not to chop on.
 Share 3d ago 01.08 EST Ivor might have found a cold corner at Bellerive Oval but Vinny in Dorset has nothing but nice things to say about Hobart.
 “You’ll struggle to find a nicer spot to spend a day watching cricket than the Bellerive Oval,” Vinny says. “Fond memories of watching Australia v Sri Lanka Test match in 2012 there. Australia’s first post Ponting Test I believe. The ‘water taxi’ across the Derwent to the Oval was a highlight too.”
 Share 3d ago 01.06 EST 37th over: England 236-5 (Duckett 122, Jacks 15) SIX! Duckett slogs Head but a top edge makes it initially seem unlikely to clear Bartlett on the rope. The opener picks up three more through cover and Jacks smacks a boundary in front of point. 17 runs from the over.
 Share 3d ago 01.01 EST Ivor is trying to take his mind off the weather as he throws up a curly one for us to ponder. “Sitting freezing to death in one of the less sunny spots at Bellerive,” he says. “Not sure if it’s been mentioned but five England players have played for the Hobart Hurricanes and no Australians. If you want to push it further, can you name them?”
 I’ll leave the floor open for now and see if anyone can get all five.
 Share 3d ago 00.59 EST 36th over: England 219-5 (Duckett 112, Jacks 8) Beardman is back in the attack. Four singles come from the opening four deliveries before Duckett cashes in on being given too much room and hammers a cut to the rope. Bartlett has been back on the field for a handful of overs after getting some attention on a leg issue. He should be able to bowl again shortly after spending time away from the action.
 Share 3d ago 00.57 EST 35th over: England 210-5 (Duckett 105, Jacks 6) Duckett returns from the beverage break showing more intent now that he has already reached his milestone. The opener slog sweeps Head from well outside off stump and over deep midwicket for four. An aggressive drive takes a thick edge and falls narrowly short of a diving Beardman in the gully to short third region.
 Share 3d ago 00.52 EST A reminder that Cricket Australia has announced the creation of an independent “forum” for players and staff to share their accounts of the infamous South Africa tour of 2018 in the hope it provides a “circuit breaker” to the ongoing sandpaper saga.
 Speaking next to a children’s playground outside Bellerive Oval in Hobart before the third one-day international between Australia and England, David Boon, the interim CA chair, and chief executive Todd Greenberg insisted the intention is not to “re-litigate” events eight years ago and it will not lead to further sanctions.
 Ali Martin was in Hobart to hear all about it …
 ‘Time for a circuit breaker’: Cricket Australia creates forum for players to air views on sandpapergate Read more Share 3d ago 00.50 EST 34th over: England 204-5 (Duckett 100, Jacks 5) Duckett reaches a hundred with a clip off the pads for one. That might mark time for him to open up again but Connolly has both the England batters on a tight leash. That’s drinks.
 Share 3d ago 00.48 EST CENTURY! for Ben Duckett
 The England opener brings up his seventh ODI century and his first in Australia (this is his first series in the country) from 94 deliveries with 13 boundaries and a six. That’s his third in his past five ODIs after arriving in Australia in top form.
 Share 3d ago 00.48 EST 33rd over: England 202-5 (Duckett 99, Jacks 4) Duckett edges closer to his ton with a pair of singles as Australia have the field back saving boundaries. Head loses his grip and a loopy delivery bounces off the pitch. Jacks opens up from the freehit but the ball flies skyward and barely 10 metres from the pitch as England scamper for two.
 Share 3d ago 00.43 EST WICKET! Archer c Edwards b Head 7 (England 195-5)
 Jofra Archer slog sweeps again but this time picks out Travis Head at deep mid-wicket. The Australian fielder races in off the rope and takes a smart catch diving forward.
 Share 3d ago 00.42 EST 32nd over: England 195-4 (Duckett 97, Archer 7) Duckett starts the over hammering Connolly through the covers for four. Archer adds a second boundary with a slog sweep from down on one knee. That’s more likely what he was sent in early to do with Australia’s spinners changing the game.
 Share 3d ago 00.39 EST 31st over: England 185-4 (Duckett 92, Archer 2) SIX! Duckett opens up to move within sight of a century. The opener smacks Renshaw back over his head for the first six of the innings. Renshaw ends the over asking the question as Archer tries to switch hit him but is rapped on the pads. Looks to be sliding down leg.
 Share 3d ago 00.36 EST 30th over: England 176-4 (Duckett 84, Archer 1) Connolly continues around the wicket to Duckett and as the opener playing off the back foot with little threat. Duckett finds a single to deep midwicket and Archer gets off the mark with an inside edge.
 Share 3d ago 00.34 EST WICKET! Cox st Inglis b Renshaw 12 (England 172-4)
 Jordan Cox dances down the track but fails to get bat on ball as he is beaten in the flight and Inglis whips off the bails. Renshaw has 2 for 24 from seven overs during a gamechanging spell. Jofra Archer comes in ahead of Will Jacks.
 29th over: England 172-4 (Duckett 82, Archer 0) 
 Share Updated at  00.34 EST 3d ago 00.30 EST 28th over: England 168-3 (Duckett 80, Cox 10) Duckett finally breaks the shackles as he reverse sweeps Connolly to the boundary. But the England opener can’t find a way through the infield again.
 Share 3d ago 00.26 EST 27th over: England 163-3 (Duckett 76, Cox 9) Renshaw keeps the squeeze on England with an over filled with variation of pace and length. Cox finds a pair of singles to mid-on, with Duckett’s one off the pads in between.
 Share 3d ago 00.24 EST 26th over: England 160-3 (Duckett 75, Cox 7) Travis Head keeps spin in the attack with England tied down through the middle overs. Cox picks up a couple of singles and Duckett adds one with a late cut.
 Share 3d ago 00.22 EST Rowan Sweeney writes in to lay the boot into the England captain. “I don’t want to hear that Harry Brook failed just now,” he says. “After today’s innings he’s more than doubled his ODI average in Australia. It’s now nearly eight!”
 Share 3d ago 00.20 EST 25th over: England 157-3 (Duckett 74, Cox 5) Connolly said this week he sees himself as a batter who bowls. The 23-year-old only bowled three overs in this series before sending down his third today. Five singles and a sweep for two to Duckett keep the scoreboard ticking over.
 Share 3d ago 00.17 EST 24th over: England 150-3 (Duckett 70, Cox 2) Johnson tidies up his figures just a touch after going for 40 runs from his first four overs. He now has 0 for 45 from six. England bookend this over with a pair of singles to bring up the 150 just short of the halfway mark.
